deep.reconstruction:
Setting. C is a category with a class W of weak equivalences and a class of distinguished monomorphisms (written ↣, 'cofibrations'). It has finite sums X∨X (= X⊔X), codiagonals ∇_X and cocartesian squares. This matches the cofibration-category set-up of the preceding page 14, where Grothendieck manipulates x⊔x ↣ y'⊔y'' with the insertions i_1, i_2. Grothendieck has built a combinatorial candidate C̃ for the localization W^{-1}C. Its morphisms are classes of zigzags; Hom_C̃(X,Y) is something like Π_0 of a category (or simplicial set) Ar_•(X,Y) of formal arrows, in the spirit of a hammock or roof calculus. A morphism of C̃ is denoted [f_0, i]. Here X →f_0 Ȳ ←i Y with i a weak equivalence, i.e. formally i^{-1}f_0. The page is the final step of proving that the canonical functor C̃ → W^{-1}C is an isomorphism.

Step 1 (top diagram): the category of factorizations is connected. Given f: X → Y, consider factorizations f = α∘f_0 with α ∈ W. Take two of them, (f_0', α') and (f_0'', α''). Form the pushout Ỹ of X∨X → Ȳ'⊔Ȳ'' along ∇_X: X∨X → X. The maps (α, α') induce φ: Ỹ → Y. Factor φ = α''∘φ_0 with φ_0 (in W or a cofibration; the reading is uncertain) and α'' ∈ W. Then f_0'' = φ_0∘g gives a third factorization receiving maps from both. This is the standard pushout/cylinder argument that the factorizations of f form a connected category.

Step 2: sections. If α, α' admit sections, then α'' admits one ("qui les reçoit"): compose a section of α with the comparison map to Ȳ''. So one reduces to comparing two factorizations joined by a morphism u: (f_0, α) → (f_0', α') in the category of factorizations. Choosing the section of α' to be i' = u∘i gives α'∘u∘i = α∘i = id.

Step 3: reduction to a choice-independence statement. The remaining point is that, for a chosen factorization, [f_0, i] does not depend on the section i. Since [f_0, i] = [id_Ȳ, i]∘(f_0, id_Ȳ), this reduces to (**).

(**) Let f: X → Y be in W and admit a section i (f∘i = 1_Y). Then the class in Π_0(Ar_•(Y,X)) of the zigzag (1_X, i), i.e. 'i^{-1}' (which should equal f), does not depend on the choice of section i.

Conclusion. Grothendieck asserts that this condition is necessary and sufficient for C̃ → W^{-1}C to be faithful, hence an isomorphism. Bijectivity on objects and fullness are presumably already established. Checking this should be easy once the functor C → C̃ is constructed carefully.

Purpose. This is the elementary proof that a combinatorial description of homotopy classes of zigzags computes the localization W^{-1}C for a category with cofibrations and weak equivalences. It belongs to his preparation (summer 1982 onward) of the localization and modelizer theory that resurfaces in Pursuing Stacks.
errors: No outright error. Sloppiness: the codomain should be Ȳ'⊔Ȳ'' (two different factorizations), and the direction and status of φ_0 (cofibration and/or in W) are not specified.
In (**) the Hom-set should be Π_0(Ar_•(Y,X)), since the zigzag (1_X, i) goes Y → X. Grothendieck writes Ar_•(X,Y), which is loose notation.

Necessity and sufficiency of (**) are asserted ('comme on doit pouvoir vérifier aisément') rather than proved. The fact that faithfulness implies isomorphism relies on unstated previous results (bijective on objects, full).

ideas.what: Connectedness of the category of factorizations f = α f_0 with α ∈ W, via pushout along the codiagonal X⊔X → X followed by a new factorization
ideas.modern_name: contractibility/connectedness of factorization categories; cylinder-object argument in cofibration categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. Brown (1973, dual fibrant-object setting); Waldhausen (1985); Quillen (1967)
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in Pursuing Stacks discussions of localizers

ideas.what: Description of W^{-1}C morphisms as Π_0 of a category/simplicial set of zigzags Ar_•(X,Y), and a criterion for C̃ → W^{-1}C to be an isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: hammock localization / Π_0 of zigzag categories; calculus of fractions up to homotopy
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks treats localizations of modelizers but not, to my knowledge, this specific lemma

ideas.what: Reduction of well-definedness to independence of the class of i^{-1} from the choice of section of a trivial map
ideas.modern_name: uniqueness up to homotopy of sections of weak equivalences
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in abstract homotopy theory (Brown, Waldhausen)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, competently executed lemma about computing a localization via zigzags in a category with cofibrations. It is standard Brown/Dwyer–Kan material, interesting only as a dated (≥ Aug 1982) trace of Grothendieck's pre-Pursuing-Stacks work on localization; nothing new for specialists.

Right margin: 'on factorise φ en α''φ_0 avec φ_0 ...(W?) et α'' ∈ W, et on prend f_0'' = φ_0 g'.
Line 1: 'Mais si α, α' ont des sections (il suffirait que α ou α' en ait), α'' (qui les reçoit) en a.'
'une flèche u: (f_0, α) → (f_0', α') dans la catégorie des factorisations de f en α f_0. Donc si on choisit la section i' pour α' comme l'image par u de la section i de α, ...'
